ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: There are two similar triangles in the image: on the left is triangle ABC, side AB is labeled 5, side BC is labeled 6, and side AC is labeled 7; on the right is triangle DEF, side DE is labeled 3. The problem gives △ABC ∼ △DEF, so according to the vertex order the correspondences are A↔D, B↔E, C↔F, therefore AB corresponds to DE. From AB=5 and DE=3, the similarity ratio from △ABC to △DEF is 3/5. The perimeter of △ABC is 5+6+7=18. The perimeters of similar triangles scale by the same similarity ratio, so the perimeter of △DEF is 18×(3/5)=10.8.

method.method_draft: Use the diagram to identify the corresponding labeled sides: the left triangle is \(\triangle ABC\) with \(AB=5\), \(BC=6\), \(AC=7\), and the right triangle is \(\triangle DEF\) with \(DE=3\). From the text, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\), so the vertex order gives \(AB \leftrightarrow DE\). Compute the scale factor from \(ABC\) to \(DEF\) as \(DE/AB=3/5\). First find the perimeter of \(ABC\): \(5+6+7=18\). Since perimeters of similar triangles scale by the same factor as side lengths, the perimeter of \(DEF\) is \(18\cdot 3/5=10.8\).

method.method_draft: Use the diagram to match corresponding sides by vertex order: \(A\leftrightarrow D\), \(B\leftrightarrow E\), \(C\leftrightarrow F\). Thus \(AB\leftrightarrow DE\), \(BC\leftrightarrow EF\), and \(AC\leftrightarrow DF\). From the text and image, \(AB=5\) and \(DE=3\), so the common ratio is \(3/5\). Find each missing side of \(\triangle DEF\): \(EF=(3/5)\cdot BC=(3/5)\cdot 6=3.6\), and \(DF=(3/5)\cdot AC=(3/5)\cdot 7=4.2\). Add the three sides of \(DEF\): \(DE+EF+DF=3+3.6+4.2=10.8\).
